newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM invites Clinton on independence day.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM invites Clinton on independence day.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda congratulated U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday on his re-election and invited him to visit New Delhi next year to join the country's 50th independence anniversary celebrations.
Deve Gowda's message, quoted by state-run Doordarshan television, said India looked forward to "further consolidation and deepening of ties" with the United States during his second term in office.
India gained freedom from British rule on August 15, 1947. The day is celebrated as the country's Independence Day.
On Wednesday, Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma had hailed Clinton's first term as a landmark in bilateral relations.

"During your presidency, cooperation between India and the United States has greatly expanded. Trade and investment have increased several fold and we have embarked on new areas of cooperation," Sharma said in a letter to Clinton.
During his first term Clinton pointedly declined to criticise India for alleged human rights abuses in Kashmir and for pursuing a nuclear weapons programme.
That did not deter Washington, however, from keeping the pressure on New Delhi on both fronts.

India, regarded as a threshold nuclear power, has refused to sign the Nuclear Non-proliferation Treaty or the recently introduced Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT), on both occasions against U.S. advice.
